item.title: CXMT To Leapfrog Samsung By ~2 Years, As It Gears Up To Introduce A DDR5 RDIMM Product That Leverages The 4F² Memory Cell Architecture Before Year-End
item.description:
Another week brings another anecdote of how China's CXMT is seemingly leveraging its newfound tech prowess to give the so-called Big Three memory players - Samsung, SK hynix, and Micron - a run for their money.

Even so, the latest anecdote is quite ambitious in its scope, delineating how CXMT is gearing up to leapfrog Samsung by around 2 years on the next-gen 4F² memory cell architecture.

CXMT is now gunning to introduce a server-geared memory product that leverages an entirely new memory cell architecture by the end of 2026, while Samsung intends to produce memory products on this new architecture only in 2028

To wit, CXMT's President, Dr. Cao Kanyu, recently delivered a speech at the 4th Integrated Chip and Chiplet Conference in Shanghai , discussing CXMT’s progress on the next-gen 4F² DRAM architecture as well as other innovative technologies such as hybrid bonding.

During the speech, Dr. Kanyu declared that CXMT will introduce a DDR5 RDIMM product based on the 4F² memory cell architecture before the end of 2026, which is around two years ahead of Samsung's roadmap for the introduction of this architecture.

For the benefit of those who might not be aware, the Registered Dual In-Line Memory Module (RDIMM) acts as a hardware buffer that holds the oncoming signals from the CPU for precisely one clock cycle before sending them onward to the memory chips, reducing electrical load and enabling server operators to plug in a higher number of high-capacity sticks of RAM into a single motherboard.

Meanwhile, the 4F² process is a next-generation memory cell architecture, where the components of a single memory cell (one transistor and one capacitor) are stacked vertically rather than horizontally. This design shift reduces the surface footprint of a single memory cell to a perfect square, which measures 4 times the minimum feature size squared (4 × F²), and consists of exactly 2 bitlines and 2 wordlines. Do note that bitlines and wordlines are the interconnect structures used to operate the transistors within each memory cell. Just by changing the structure to 4F², DRAM makers are able to increase the cell density of each IC by 30 - 50 percent .

Of course, CXMT has been exploring this technology for a number of years, having published its first paper on the 4F² architecture back in 2021. Also, by going from a 6F² to 4F² architecture, CXMT would be able to cut the memory cell area by around 33 percent at the same feature size, necessitating new transistors. Even so, it is quite likely that CXMT's initial implementation would be a partial derivative of the 4F² architecture on its new 15nm G5 DRAM process.

What's more, to overcome process miniaturization constraints, CXMT is now apparently using High-k Metal Gate or HKMG technology , which replaces the old silicon-based insulator with a material like hafnium oxide (HfO₂), not only curbing current leakage and the attendant waste thermal energy, but also enhancing power efficiency and paving the way for higher speeds, as the transistors are able to flip states much faster than what would have been possible via polysilicon gates. CXMT is now apparently applying this technology to its G4 DRAM fabrication process - which is widely believed to be on the 1z node - as well as LPDDR5X products.

Do note that CXMT is aggressively expanding its capacity right now, to the tune of 300,000 wafers per month - via three 300mm DRAM fabs with a capacity of ~100,000 wafers per month each - by the end of this year. It will also have an HBM-focused capacity of around 50,000 wafers per month by the end of 2026.

What's more, the memory maker is currently building two new fabs in Shanghai and Hefei, which would increase its production capacity to 600,000 wafers per month . In fact, CXMT is now on course to overtake Micron in volume production by 2030.

Elsewhere, Samsung will likely introduce the 4F² architecture with its B1b process - its first sub-10nm DRAM fabrication process and officially renamed D0a - where the memory cells and the surrounding driver circuitry, known as the peri, will be fabricated on separate wafers and then joined together via wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding, thereby stacking the memory cells on top of the peri. Because hybrid bonding is quite expensive, it is only reasonable to assume that Samsung will price the next-gen DRAM at an eye-watering premium.

item.title: Squadron 42 Storms Onto Steam With Surprisingly Low Minimum PC Requirements, but Fans Still Face a Wait Until Q2 2027
item.description:
Cloud Imperium Games has just opened Squadron 42 's Steam page , and to celebrate the occasion, they also released a brand new trailer.

Squadron 42 is the long-awaited single player campaign of Star Citizen , the highly ambitious sci-fi space simulation game that broke all crowdfunding records (it currently stands at 1.050 billion dollars and counting). The single player standalone title envisioned by Chris Roberts (Wing Commander, Starlancer, Freelancer) includes a cast that is a veritable Hollywood's Who's Who, including Mark Hamill , Gary Oldman , Gillian Anderson , Ben Mendelsohn , Henry Cavill , Andy Serkis , John Rhys-Davies , Jonathan Bailey , Mark Strong , Alix Wilton Reagan , Damson Idris , Liam Cunningham , Jane Perry , and more.

Squadron 42 promises an immersive narrative experienced through the eyes of a novice United Empire of Earth (UEE) Navy officer. Unlike Star Citizen's dynamic, open-ended universe, Squadron 42 concentrates on delivering a compelling story-driven campaign that chronicles one soldier's journey as galactic tensions escalate toward conflict.

In 2945, the UEE faces an existential crisis as outlaws and hostile extraterrestrial forces threaten from the outer reaches of space . Players join the UEE Navy as a rookie, beginning an intense odyssey that transforms them from an inexperienced recruit into a pivotal player in an interstellar conflict. Assigned to a colossal capital ship, they'll operate alongside a vibrant crew, establish meaningful connections, and navigate the difficult choices and critical decisions that will define their reputation, rank, and legacy.

Adventurers will traverse sprawling capital vessels and vibrant space stations, venture into isolated frontier settlements, and thrust into active war zones, meeting compelling characters and overcoming obstacles that forge their character's heroic identity. Cloud Imperium Games additionally boasts that Squadron 42's campaign transcends traditional flight simulation . Players will execute blistering aerial combat sequences, participate in planetary assault missions, endure catastrophic engagements, and navigate dilemmas requiring tactical thinking beyond raw combat capability.

Combining monumental set pieces with an intimate, character-driven narrative, Squadron 42 moves seamlessly between intense space combat, ground operations, and quieter moments with the people behind the fight . Every mission brings new challenges, with players relying on skill, strategy, and quick thinking as they bravely stand against the forces threatening the Empire’s future.

Leveraging StarEngine , Cloud Imperium Games' cutting-edge proprietary platform, Squadron 42 features photorealistic environments, boundless vistas, lifelike character performances, and fluid transitions between narrative cinematics and player-controlled sequences.

The Steam page lists the minimum requirements, which are very low:

  • Processor - Quad Core CPU - Intel: i7 (Sandy Bridge or later), AMD: Bulldozer or later
  • Memory - 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics - DirectX 11.1 compatible Graphics Card with 8 GB VRAM, DirectX Version 12
  • Storage - 150 GB available space

Squadron 42 was already "feature complete" three years ago , when it entered a long polishing phase. In October 2024, Cloud Imperium Games announced it was targeting a 2026 release window; however, the story-driven game was delayed to Q2 2027 , allegedly due to GTA 6 's November 19 launch date.

It's worth noting that CIG finally allowed some fans and content creators to play the game earlier this week. The first community hands-on sessions have produced broadly positive early impressions, with attendees praising its cinematic presentation, livelier combat, and detailed environments. However, the accounts also suggest that players expecting the freedom of Star Citizen should prepare for a considerably more directed experience for the standalone title.

At Cloud Imperium Games' Manchester event, selected backers and content creators were given around five hours to play at their own pace. Reddit user NackteElfe described impressive facial detail and character models, alongside a densely populated world where NPCs appeared occupied with their own activities . The attendee felt that Roberts' ambition to recreate the Wing Commander experience came through, although the presentation sometimes felt linear.

Combat was another highlight. According to the same attendee, e nemies attempted to flank the player and revive fallen allies, while hits against the Vanduul delivered convincing physical feedback . Space battles also impressed, particularly the ship destruction enabled by CIG's Maelstrom technology. Sound design received praise for making the experience feel grand and vibrant.

The session was not exclusively about shooting or dogfighting. Players encountered hacking and continued discovering mechanics several hours into the demo . Other reactions nevertheless raised concerns about the amount of cinematics and the prevalence of slower, heavily directed sequences, suggesting that pacing could prove divisive.

Bugs were present, too. NackteElfe considered them consistent with a game approaching its final polishing stages, but that's just an individual opinion. So far, the broader takeaway seems to be one of cautious optimism : these selected community impressions suggest that Squadron 42 is delivering an entertaining, cinematic campaign, with technical polish and pacing still worth watching.

item.title: AMD Hikes GDDR6 Prices For Partners Starting October 1st, While NVIDIA Reportedly Holds Off On GDDR7
item.description:
Multiple Radeon GPU families utilize the GDDR6 memory chips, but it's likely that the RDNA 4 lineup will end up being affected the most.

Starting This Month, AMD Implements Another Memory Price Hike for GDDR6-Based GPUs, But It's Not the Only Thing That Will Increase GPU Prices

Memory prices must have climbed once again recently, which is why we are now hearing that AMD has implemented another price hike for memory. Board Channels reports that AMD has already raised the prices for its GDDR6 memory for its board partners, which means board partners will now have no other option but to pass the costs on to consumers.

Apparently, memory prices have become the major factor in recent GPU price hikes, but it's not the only factor contributing to such hikes. According to Bench Life , there have been price hikes for numerous components such as SMD components and PCBs. All of them are contributing to the recent price hikes, but memory remains the most affected component.

Considering AMD has raised GDDR6 memory prices, it means that it's going to affect multiple Radeon GPU families. GDDR6 has been used in the Radeon RX 5000, 6000, and 7000 series, and the current RDNA 4-based Radeon RX 9000 series. Given that some earlier generations have already been discontinued or are seeing lower production, it's the Radeon RX 9000 series that will be affected the most.

The report states that AMD has already notified its board partners about the memory price hike, which it implemented on October 1st . On the other hand, NVIDIA hasn't notified its partners about a memory price hike . NVIDIA ships GDDR7 to its partners, which is more expensive than GDDR6, and this has already caused a significant increase in RTX 50 series prices.

However, it's stated that NVIDIA may not raise the memory prices this year. Well, we have already seen that the RTX 50 series has witnessed noticeably sharper price hikes than RDNA 4 GPUs, and another price hike could be brutal.

item.title: US-Based System Integrator Says GPU Prices Are Expected To Soar Significantly, Making It Difficult To Secure Enough Inventory
item.description:
The GPU market is about to get worse as system integrators are expecting more price hikes in the coming days.

Stince Built Expects Higher GPU Prices in the Near Future as Supply Constraints Tighten Their Grip While Memory Availability Worsens

Many vendors have been reportedly struggling to maintain sufficient inventory for PC components like memory, SSDs, and GPUs. This has been going on for nearly one year now, thanks to the RAMpocalypse era that started last year. Not just memory and SSDs have hit all-time-high prices; GPUs have started to become almost unaffordable these days. Looks like the situation could get even worse in the coming months.

US-based system integrator Stince Built has stated that GPU availability is limited. The post mentions that it is becoming extremely difficult for the vendor to secure enough GPUs for their PC builds. With growing memory demand for AI and data centers, component pricing and availability have been affected drastically. While the memory and SSDs were already causing a lot of problems for this vendor, the GPU shortage is now another major factor that could lead to higher prices for its PC builds.

Stince Built says that it expects GPU prices to climb "significantly" and that these elevated prices could persist for a longer time. This means the vendor won't have any other choice but to pass the increased costs to its customers. GPUs have already risen by nearly 50-60% in price compared to last year, with some GPUs now hitting End of Life. We have already heard earlier today that NVIDIA has reportedly ended production of the RTX 5090 , as it now aims to keep the GB202 strictly for the RTX PRO series.

The rest of the RTX 50 series SKUs have already witnessed multiple price jumps this year, making them almost unaffordable. Stince Built says that it's trying to secure GPU inventory to keep the costs down, but we know this won't be easy. Recently, AMD also announced one more price hike for its GPUs, and that will further create difficulties for both system integrators like Stince Built and the consumers.

item.title: Intel’s Arrow Lake Ends Up Inside A 2Crsi Edge Security Camera, Packing Arc 130T Graphics That Could Theoretically Run Games
item.description:
This is probably the only surveillance camera that can theoretically play video games, thanks to the Arrow Lake SoC.

2Crsi Edge Deploys Intel Core Ultra 5 225H Inside Vision Guard Security Camera With Local AI Capabilities

Hardware has evolved so much that it now gets its way into devices you wouldn't have imagined a few years ago. One such product is 2Crsi Edge's new surveillance camera that brings consumer-grade hardware for advanced security measures. As spotted by @FanlessTech , the vendor 2Crsi Edge has made the Vision Guard VG-15MV-66 surveillance camera that brings an Intel Arrow Lake processor.

The spec sheet listed on the official website mentions the Intel Core 5 225H, a budget-oriented processor with 14 cores through 4 Performance + 8 Efficient core configuration and up to a 4.9 GHz boost speed. I think it's already overkill for a surveillance camera, but that's what makes it stand out when it comes to regular surveillance devices. The Core 5 225H makes more sense for multi-camera AI surveillance system.

And this one isn't a a simple computer for recording camera footage, but it's an edge-computing system designed to process video and run AI models locally. The system can deliver up to 214 TOPS of AI power through an optional Axelera Metis AI accelerator, which can run supported neural networks for tasks such as object detection and classification. On the other hand, the powerful Arc 130T integrated graphics can assist with supported graphics or video-processing workloads.

So, it's an advanced security camera that not only does its job better than conventional models but can theoretically play games as well. Arc 130T is known for its good performance in less-intensive titles, and while we don't know if running games on this device is possible through workarounds, it surely looks capable of running games.

That said, its manufacturer has kept it strictly for surveillance, and it is ideal for streetlights, utility poles, or roadside structures to power cameras and process their video feeds without sending everything to a central server.

News Source: 2Crsi Edge

item.title: Microsoft’s Overhauled XBOX PC App Is Reportedly Much Faster, With a Redesigned Interface and Improved Navigation
item.description:
Microsoft is reportedly preparing a major overhaul of its XBOX PC app , with a redesigned interface and substantial performance improvements aimed at addressing some of the longstanding complaints surrounding the company's gaming ecosystem on Windows.

According to a new report from Windows Central , Microsoft is internally testing a rebuilt version of the XBOX PC app, codenamed Garrison . The publication's Jez Corden managed to get his hands on an early build, sharing a video demonstration highlighting the improvements.

The most immediately noticeable change is reportedly a substantial boost in responsiveness , particularly when navigating large game libraries. Corden, whose XBOX library contains more than 1,400 titles , observed significantly faster loading times compared to the existing application.

While no precise performance benchmarks were provided, the improvements appear promising for PC gamers who have long criticized the XBOX app for its sluggish navigation, slow library loading, and occasionally cumbersome interface.

Beyond performance, Microsoft has also streamlined the application's navigation and overall design. Previously, the XBOX app maintained separate pages for game listings and their corresponding store pages. The redesigned version consolidates both into a single interface , reducing unnecessary navigation and making it easier to browse games, manage purchases, and access additional information.

Meanwhile, The Verge's Tom Warren has also shared some screenshots of the redesigned XBOX PC app, offering another look at its refreshed interface. Warren remarked that the new design is "coming along nicely" and confirmed that performance is "definitely better" than the current version, further corroborating Windows Central's early impressions. The screenshots also highlight Microsoft's efforts to deliver a cleaner, more streamlined gaming experience on Windows.

Another welcome improvement is clearer differentiation between games that can be installed locally and those available exclusively through XBOX Cloud Gaming . This should help eliminate some confusion when browsing large libraries containing titles from multiple XBOX generations.

The new app also supports both mouse-and-keyboard and controller-based navigation , with an interface that automatically adjusts its scaling for controller use. Furthermore, users can configure it as their default home screen when entering Windows 11's new gaming-focused mode, making it particularly suitable for handheld gaming PCs such as the ROG XBOX Ally .

However, this is still an early build, and the overhaul currently focuses primarily on performance and usability rather than introducing substantial new functionality. Features such as community tools, developer interaction, user reviews, and improved store discovery remain areas where Microsoft's offering continues to trail Valve's Steam.

As for availability, Microsoft has yet to announce an official release date , although Corden believes the redesigned XBOX PC app could reach Xbox Insiders in the coming weeks, potentially before the end of 2026.

Considering Microsoft's renewed emphasis on PC gaming, XBOX Play Anywhere, and handheld gaming devices, the Garrison overhaul could represent a meaningful step toward making the XBOX app a more competitive PC gaming platform. Whether it can eventually challenge Steam's considerably richer ecosystem, however, remains to be seen.

News Sources: Windows Central , Tom Warren , via VideoCardz

item.title: Starfield Players Wanted No Man’s Sky-Style Seamless Landings Since Launch, but Now a Singer-Songwriter, Not a Coder, Is Building Them
item.description:
An upcoming Starfield mod aims to introduce what many players have wanted since launch: seamless landings on planets, ala No Man's Sky or Star Citizen .

Interestingly, it's being developed by someone who's not a coder by profession at all. According to his own webpage , Frederik Wessberg is a Danish singer-songwriter and audio engineer, yet he made this his passion project over the last six months or so. Here's his technical explanation, which leverages Starfield's hidden "true space simulator" capabilities:

I thought it would be a fun small project, but I quickly realized how wrong I was. Because planet rendering in Space in vanilla Starfield is very limited: a planet is represented by a texture, maybe a moving cloud layer, and maybe an atmosphere. Flying closer to it than the game allows will mean flying into a flat texture and eventually losing atmospheric rendering.

So, to build actual seamless landings, I had to completely reimplement Starfield's planet rendering in space in 3D, in a way that looks detailed and sharp at every altitude. Thankfully, Starfield is actually amazingly physically accurate, and in many ways a true space simulator - it just doesn't ever reveal this to the player, but I could leverage it in my design here.

So, the planet rendering is based upon Starfield's biome data and exact surface maps, including climate data, atmospheric composition data, and takes into account things like orbital phase, distance to the sun, distance to the moon(s) orbiting the planet, and how they contribute to moonlight, and so on. The philosophy is: Starfield's data is the "truth", but we then modulate it by real physics.

As shown in the video demonstration, the seamless landings can be autopiloted, but the player can also fly manually and even land on water . Moreover, during the landing phase, Starfield players will actually navigate authentic 3D volumetric cloud formations shaped by climate data and dynamic weather systems, complete with thunderstorms and lightning strikes, polar auroras, night-side airglow, and scientifically accurate atmospheric scattering derived from the game's atmospheric composition data.

There are even city lights emanating from points of interest on the surface, expansive terrain, and cloud shadows rendered globally, authentic biomes, oceans, and ice-covered peaks generated from the game's native data and surface cartography. The ship's re-entry heat shield also produces realistic fume effects against the hull and deposits an ash layer accordingly .

The Starfield Seamless Landing mod is still a work in progress, and there's no ETA on its release yet. However, Wessberg already clarified that it will be PC-only and require SFSE , the game's Script Extender that powers most of the biggest mods.

Back in March, Bethesda Game Studios released the Free Lanes update, Terran Armada DLC, and PlayStation 5 version. In July, when the studio provided its updated long-term roadmap for all the franchises , Bethesda also clarified that work on Starfield was far from done , with new stories, gameplay improvements, Starborn content, and additional updates coming in 2027.

item.title: Samsung & SK hynix Have Set A Dangerous Greed Cycle That Has Trickled Down To Suppliers Like ASML, Who Now Want To Match Their Customers’ Profit Margins
item.description:
The profits being raked in by Samsung and SK hynix during the DRAM shortage have made both memory manufacturers the source of envy amongst high-profile suppliers like ASML, which is now reportedly seeking a price hike to match what its clients are generating in annual net earnings. According to the latest report, the changes have been finalized, setting a perilous precedent across the entire industry.

ASML is reportedly charging a flat 10 percent higher fee for every EUV and DUV part, with Samsung and SK hynix seemingly having agreed

The Dutch equipment manufacturer is raising prices for all replacement parts found in its machines. According to The Elec, these changes are expected to take effect in January 2027, with the proposal reportedly sent to both Samsung and SK hynix through their Korean subsidiaries last month. Given the scale at which both manufacturers are generating profits, they likely felt that a 10 percent price hike was a drop in the bucket, so based on the fresh details, they agreed.

Both EUV and DUV equipment have a plethora of moving parts that are susceptible to wear and tear over time. These parts include photolithography equipment, optical paraphernalia such as lenses, mirrors, light sources, and precision actuators. With every single one of these parts obtaining a 10 percent price hike, it’s clear that, being the only manufacturer of advanced EUV machinery, ASML doesn’t wish to get left behind during the AI boom and wants the same opportunity as Samsung and SK hynix when it comes to printing money.

In fact, one unnamed industry source has noted that while prices have risen across an entire spectrum of components, ASML seeks a larger margin to match what its customers, Samsung and SK hynix, are making. The Dutch firm has forecasted that its revenue would increase by more than 30 percent this year, and that’s without the price hike initiated. Additionally, Chinese customers who intend to purchase DUV equipment will also have to pay an additional 10 percent.

Given that the entire industry wants an upper hand in the AI race, these clients have agreed to the hike. While ASML is part of the industry responsible for mass-producing cutting-edge wafers, it hasn’t been adversely impacted by memory and NAND flash shortages, so it’s clear the company wants to capitalize in the same way as Samsung and SK hynix. Unfortunately, this practice has set off a chain reaction spreading through the entire industry.

Companies like Applied Materials and Japan’s Tokyo Electron have increased the price of their products, and with this cycle seeing no end, consumers are going to receive the short end of the stick.

News Source: The Elec

item.title: GMKtec EVO-X3 “AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395” Mini PC Review: Enhanced Cooling In A Local AI Powerhouse
item.description:
Product Info
GMKtec EVO X3
August, 2026
Type
Mini PC
Price
$3799.99

GMKtec has been making Mini PCs for years now. They are based out of the technology hub of Shenzhen, China, and have maintained strategic partnerships with AMD, Intel & Microsoft, and currently offer a wide array of solutions, all the way from entry-level to enthusiast-grade designs based on mobility chips from AMD & Intel.

The latest offering from GMKtek that targets high-end users is the EVO X3, a compact design that is equipped with AMD's Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (internally codenamed Strix Halo). This SoC takes everything we know about Strix "Ryzen AI 300" series, takes it into overdrive mode with a chiplet architecture, and offers incredibly powerful specs.

The GMKtec EVO X3 not only houses the top Strix Halo APU, but it also features a wide array of IO and a strong set of internal specs, such as storage and memory. The PC is a full-on upgrade to the original Ryzen AI MAX+ design offered by GMKtec, the EVO X2 .

GMKtec EVO X3 Mini PC - Specifications At A Glance

In terms of specifications, the GMKtec EVO X3 is equipped with the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 APU. This is the flagship processor within the Strix Halo lineup, which is purpose-built as a Mini Workstation platform and has a lot to talk about, so let's get started.

The AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 APU features 16 cores in total with 32 threads, and is based on TSMC's 4nm process technology. Unlike the standard Strix lineup, which mixes Zen 5 and Zen 5C cores, the Strix Halo family features the full-fledged, high-performance Zen 5C cores. These 16 cores are packaged within two Core Complexes, or CCX chiplets, each housing 8 cores and 32 MB of L3 cache for a total of 64 MB & 16 MB of L2 on the CPU side.

The CPU has a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The Zen 5 cores clock up to 5.1 GHz and have a TDP rating of 55W at default, which can be configured down to 54W and up to 140W. The SoC is featured on the FP11 platform and is BGA in design.

For the iGPU, AMD is using its latest RDNA 3.5 architecture, which is a slightly upgraded & more efficient variant of the RDNA 3 architecture.

The AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 features a massive integrated GPU core on the same interposer that is located within its IOD chiplet. This GPU is massive because it features 40 compute units, up from 12 CUs on the top Ryzen AI 300 "Strix" APU. The GPU clocks in at a maximum frequency of 2900 MHz.

The RDNA 3.5 iGPUs support all the latest APIs and AI Frameworks. Plus, RDNA 3.5 also supports the latest upscaling and frame generation features, such as FSR 2, FSR 3, FSR 3 Frame-Gen, FSR 4, and AFMF2, while adding advanced latency reduction technologies such as Anti-Lag 2. It's one of the fastest iGPUs on the market right now.

On the NPU side, the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 is equipped with an XDNA 2 NPU, which offers a peak TOPS of 50 and supports all the latest AI frameworks. This is the fastest NPU in terms of AI TOPS in the market right now, and the only thing that comes close is the 48 TOPS of the Lunar Lake lineup. But since there's also a massive GPU at disposal, the SoC offers a total AI compute of 126 TOPS.

AMD Ryzen AI 300 APUs:

Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 375 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 12/24 2.0 / 5.1 GHz 36 MB / 24 MB L3 85 AI TOPs (55 TOPS NPU) Radeon 890M (16 CU @ 2.9 GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)
Ryzen AI 9 HX 375 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 12/24 2.0 / 5.1 GHz 36 MB / 24 MB L3 Radeon 890M (16 CU @ 2.9 GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)
Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 12/24 2.0 / 5.1 GHz 36 MB / 24 MB L3 85 AI TOPs (55 TOPS NPU) Radeon 890M (16 CU @ 2.9 GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)
Ryzen AI 9 HX PRO 370 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 12/24 2.0 / 5.1 GHz 36 MB / 24 MB L3 80 AI TOPs (50 TOPS NPU) Radeon 890M (16 CU @ 2.9 GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)
Ryzen AI 7 365 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 10/20 2.0 / 5.0 GHz 30 MB / 20 MB L3 80 AI TOPs (50 TOPS NPU) Radeon 880M (12 CU @ 2.9 GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)
Ryzen AI 7 PRO 360 Zen 5 / Zen 5C 8/16 2.0 / 5.0 GHz 24 MB / 16 MB L3 80 AI TOPs (50 TOPS NPU) Radeon 880M (12 CU @ TBD GHz) 28W (cTDP 15-54W)

With the internals of the SoC covered, let's talk about the rest of the specifications. First, we have the memory, which comes in the form of 128 GB of LPDDR5x. The Mini PC comes pre-configured and pre-soldered in the 128 GB option. The LPDDR5x modules on the GMKtek EVO X3 operate at 8000 MT/s (Micron) across a 256-bit wide bus interface.

This wider memory bus is available on AMD's Ryzen AI MAX+ APUs, allowing for up to 256 GB/s of bandwidth. This is essential since the GPU itself only has 32 MB of cache onboard, which means that the LPDDR5x subsystem is what will be used as the primary means of communication.

LPDDR5x is fast, but we expect that AMD will move to the newer LPDDR6 standards as soon as the next-gen Halo chips arrive to further offset the bandwidth requirements. The RDNA 3.5 architecture also has a decent memory compression algorithm, which can reduce some of the bandwidth needs.

The biggest advantage of Strix Halo APUs is that you can dedicate large pools of memory to the iGPU, making them a strong solution for LLMs. Our solution can dedicate up to 96 GB of memory to the iGPU alone, showing it as a GPU with 96 GB of available VRAM. This makes for a strong AI solution and an even better gaming platform where graphics memory limitations can be bypassed by simply dedicating more system memory to the iGPU.

Our review unit was equipped with a 2 TB Crucial PCIe Gen4 SSD with a dedicated heatsink. The EVO X3 has two M.2 Gen4x4 slots, which can be equipped with 8 TB each for up to 16 TB of SSD capacity.

IO includes a USB4 Type-C (40 Gbps) port, a USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A port, a USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-A port, a USB 2.0 port, a 3.5mm combo audio jack, an HDMI 2.1 display output, a 2.5GbE LAN port, an OCuLink port, a DC Power input port, and a power button. The OCuLink port supports a full PCIe Gen4x4 interface and supports the latest AMD/NVIDIA discrete graphics cards.

Talking a little bit about the BIOS, it is very barebones for the EVO X3. The first page lists various information about the Mini PC and has one important setting, the "Power Mode Select". This gives three options: Performance mode with a 140W target, Balanced mode with an 85W target, and Quiet mode with a 54W target. In the advanced menu, you can find the graphics options, where you can enable UMA to set a custom frame buffer size for the GPU.

There are other CPU options too in the Advanced menu, but nothing that can further overclock the chip itself. The memory configuration options let you select "Auto" or manual clock speeds. These only go below the factory 8000 MT/s speeds. And finally, we have the fan speed control options. These can also be set using a fan mode button on the Mini PC itself.

GMKtec EVO X3 Mini PC - Unboxing & A Closer Look

The GMKtec EVO X3 comes inside a large package with a gold GMKtec logo engraved on the front.

The back of the box has some basic specifications that list the specific configuration for this model. We got the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 variant with 128 GB of memory and a 2 TB SSD.

Within the box, you can find the Mini PC in its old compartment, along with a guide/warranty booklet, the power adapter, the power cable, and an HDMI cable. The adapter is made by Huntkey with the specific model number being "HKA230195A2-0A7" and offers up to 230.1W of power to the system.

GMKtec's Mini PCs really do stand out from the rest of the market offerings, with a stylish dual-tone design. Unlike the EVO X2, the X3 goes with a vertical and slimmer layout instead of the box design. It comes with ventilation ports on the front, back, and sides. The sides also have a few exhaust vents and feature a green color.

The Mini PC is fully enclosed on the sides. All the air it receives is from the top and the front.

The front I/O on the GMKtec NucBox EVO X3 Mini PC comes with a Power Button, a headphone jack, a USB 3.2 Gen1, and a USB 2.0 Type-A port configuration. The power button lights up when the PC is running.

The back I/O includes a single USB4 Type-C 40 Gbps port, a single USB 3.2 Gen2 Type-A port, a single HDMI 2.1 port, one 2.5GbE port, & a DC-In power port. The OCuLink port is also featured on the back.

The back side has large vents for cooling.

There are three fans within the EVO X3. One on the front and two on the back. Opening up the chassis is simple which involves the removal of 8 screws from the back and two screws from the sides. Opening up the back metal frame, you are greeted with the internal PCB and the cooling solution.

The system features two Micron 128 GB DDR5-8000 LPDDR5X memory modules. The SSD is from Micron too. There are two M.2 slots, with both housing a 2280 form factor device. The heatsink is a triple-heat pipe design which is said to sustain up to 140W of TDP.

The AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ systems we have tested so far have been very impressive in all regards. The EVO X2 from GMKtec was and remains the fastest system within our Mini PC test suite, & the tradition continues with the EVO X3.

The EVO X3 feels mightier in all regards, with better performance, better cooling, and more power headroom. The 140W mode gave us a further 10-15% uplift in CPU and 5-10% uplift in gaming workloads. The AI performance remains top-notch, and this is the first time that we tested the Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 inside a Mini PC with 128 GB of memory. This enormous pool enables LLMs with larger parameters, and the performance was fantastic.

One of the biggest upgrades comes in the form of the cooling, which now features a design similar to a laptop with two blower-type fans and one supplementary fan. This allows GMKtec to crank up the TDP all the way up to 140W, a 20W uplift over the EVO X2. Price-wise, the EVO X3 retails at $3799, which puts it in the ultra-premium range. The 64 GB EVO X2 was at $1499 when we tested it last year, but things have changed a lot. The GMKtec EVO X3 is a phenomenal machine for running AI locally. It handles those with its massive 128 GB memory with ease; plus, it has the CPU and GPU horsepower for gaming and content creation. item.title: NVIDIA Reportedly Axes RTX 5090 Production, Diverting GB202 Chips To PRO Cards As Gamers Get An RTX 5080 24 GB
item.description:
NVIDIA is reportedly ending production of the RTX 5090 and will now introduce a new model for enthusiasts, the RTX 5080 24 GB.

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 50 Lineup To Get Major Changes Soon, RTX 5080 24 GB Replaces RTX 5090 32 GB

The NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 launched back in January 2025, and there have been many reports of the card getting EOL'd or facing production cuts, but none of them have been conclusive so far .

Well, it looks like a new round of reports is surfacing, according to which the GeForce RTX 5090 production will soon cease to exist. As per insiders, the RTX 5090 will no longer be produced, and the GB202 GPU it utilizes will instead be supplied solely to the RTX Pro lineup.

If we look at the current RTX landscape, the GB202 GPU is the flagship chip within the Blackwell lineup. On the gaming front, it is featured on the 32 GB RTX 5090, which is the fastest graphics card for gamers on the market right now. On the professional front, the same chip serves three graphics cards: the 96 GB RTX PRO 6000, the 84 GB RTX PRO 5500, and the 72/48 GB RTX PRO 5000.

One can easily tell why NVIDIA wants to refocus its GB202 Blackwell chip on the Pro front. The RTX 5090 has already reached prices north of $6000 , and this is already Pro-tier pricing. DRAM continues to increase in terms of prices, and demand for AI continues to jump, this might have pushed NVIDIA to refocus its current supply of GB202 chips to Pro cards instead of gaming RTX cards.

The RTX PRO variants have also seen a massive surge in prices. This pushed many AI customers to get RTX 5090 32 GB GPUs instead, since they still offered better value. China and regions where these GPUs are banned are already retrofitting 1000s of smuggled 5090s with modified coolers and PCBs that make them viable for AI workstations and servers.

The reason this is happening despite there being export-compliant variants such as the RTX PRO 6000D and RTX 5090D V2 available is that those variants come with locked features, massive AI compute cuts, and lower memory .
